verdict.line: You lose if Mordekaiser lands Death's Grasp into an all-in before level 6; you win if you survive to the mid-late game where your build and Q's true damage take over, matching Gwen's 51% win rate across 859 games.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's E (Death's Grasp) is a low-cooldown area pull (16/14/12/10/8s) that lets him force trades on his terms, and his passive (Darkness Rise) rewards him for landing three hits in those trades with a damage aura and move speed. Gwen has no hard CC to punish that all-in, so the matchup's defensive shape comes from her having to lean on W's targeting restriction and E's dash to survive rather than contest trades directly. Once his low-cooldown tools and level 6 ultimate threat pass, Gwen's stacking true damage and scaling build close the gap, which is why the matchup sits near even by the numbers despite the early and solo-kill edge going to him.

theirWindow.when: After he lands Death's Grasp on you
theirWindow.what: He's pulled you into range to start landing hits toward his passive's third-hit payoff. Pop W immediately and look to disengage with E rather than trading back into a stacking aura.

yourWindow.when: His Q and E are both down
yourWindow.what: Dash in with E for the attack speed, range, and on-hit magic damage buff, land a hit to refund part of its cooldown, then chain Q snips for true damage and A Thousand Cuts healing before he has an answer.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: The ability-power and mana sustain let you keep farming with Q from max range through his Obliterate and Death's Grasp pokes without needing to recall early.

boots.why: Magic penetration pushes your Q true-damage center hits and A Thousand Cuts procs harder, which matters more than raw mitigation once his E/Q cooldowns are this short.

core.why: Appears in every top build path for this matchup and gives the early stat foundation to survive his level 1-5 trading window.
Sustain through extended trades matters here since he can out-stack passive damage on you if the fight drags without it.
Punishes his low-HP windows after you've chipped him down with Q snips and R needles.

situational.when: you're ahead and snowballing, for burst amplification
you want sustained attack speed dps instead of a second burst item
you need to survive a dive or dodge the follow-up after Realm of Death
the enemy team stacks additional hard cc beyond Death's Grasp

runes.keystoneWhy: The stacking adaptive damage and healing reward the exact trade pattern this lane forces: repeated Q snips and E dash-ins during extended melee exchanges where he's also trying to sustain off Indestructible.

summoners.why: This is the dominant pick in the data (65% win rate, 83.3% pick rate) because Ignite punishes his W (Indestructible) healing and closes out trades before he can shield it off, while Flash covers the gap when his E pull catches you out of position.

playing.title: Respect the E pull angle
playing.detail: Death's Grasp pulls all enemies in its area toward him, so standing near jungle entrances or walls just lets him land it for free. Stay centered in lane so he has to walk through minions to threaten it.

playing.title: Don't trade right after his Q or E lands
playing.detail: His Q (Obliterate) is only 8/7/6/5/4s cooldown, so one cast landing doesn't mean he's defenseless. Wait until both his Q and E are visibly down before committing your E dash.

playing.title: Dash in on his downtime, not yours
playing.detail: Use E (Skip 'n Slash) to engage when his cooldowns are gone, land a hit to refund part of E's own cooldown, then chain Q snips for true damage and healing.

playing.title: Drop W when he commits
playing.detail: Hallowed Mist means only enemies who enter it can target you. Place it and back off so he either wastes time walking in or the fight is deterred outright.

playing.title: Play around his ultimate from level 6
playing.detail: Realm of Death can isolate and duel you alone, and if he kills you there he keeps your stolen stats. Don't overextend past mid lane alone once it's up.

playing.title: Spread your R casts across a fight
playing.detail: Needlework can be recast up to two more times. Save the extra casts for when he's grouped with minions or allies so the slow and A Thousand Cuts application lands on more targets instead of dumping all three into one trade.

playing.title: Farm through the early deficit
playing.detail: Lane and solo-kill advantage sit with him through level 11, so prioritize safe CS with max-range Q over forced trades. The lane evens out once Dusk and Dawn into Riftmaker and Shadowflame come online.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, summoners, and all win/pick-rate numbers above are pulled from measured Gwen vs Mordekaiser top lane games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and lane timing calls are my own analysis, not measured data.
